summary:
# NOTES: GIRL SCOUTS IN ARIZONA AND NEW MEXICO
Author: Lillian Elizabeth Roy (1923, Grosset & Dunlap). Single book, 17 chapters.

## CHARACTERS
- **Mrs. Vernon** ("Verny", Captain, founded Dandelion Troop, Elmertown). **Mr. Vernon** ("Unk Verny", "Uncle Verny").
- **Mr. Gilroy** ("Gilly", "Gilly-of-the-Dandelioners", "Boss" to Tally; Denver; Adirondack estate; rich host; Rockies host). Says "Great Scott."
- **Scouts:**
  - Juliet "Julie" Lee: Leader, twin, secret journalist for *Elmertown Record*, photographer, flirt, vivacious.
  - Elizabeth "Betty" Lee: twin, timid, gullible, "Gilly, dear."
  - Joan Allison: Corporal, scribe, "Jo," wry humor.
  - Hester Wynant ("Hesty"/"Hessie"): camera operator.
  - Anne Bailey: big eater; sister Eleanor marries Henry last week of July.
  - Amy Ward: mother Mrs. Ward; joins late.
  - Judith ("Judy") and Edith Blake: Mrs. Blake forbids. Judith joins late; Edith stays home.
  - Ruth Bentley: to Paris with parents.
- **Tally:** Indian guide, broken English ("Me," "Mees Jule," "Boss"). Loves Mrs. Vernon.
- **Tom Sanderson ("Sandy"/"Sandy"):** Forest Ranger, U. of Albuquerque graduate, Panchuelo post. Horse Snubby. Pro-Pueblo; hates hunting for sport. Courts Julie.
- **Mr. Burt:** newspaper correspondent from Chicago. Pueblo/Bursum Bill articles. Later goes to Zuñi.
- **Ranger Johnson ("Johnny"):** Grass Mountain. **Ranger Oliver:** his pal.
- **Victor Adair** (dark, slender, witty) and **Godfrey Chase** (blond, good-natured): college men with thoroughbreds.
- **Padre Miguel:** 88, Santa Fé priest.
- **Mr. Balmore:** Denver gentleman at Laguna.
- **Mr. Walters:** manager, El Navajo hotel, Gallup.
- **Lorenzo "Lo":** Navajo guide.
- **Ben and Bill:** horse thieves.
- **John Sweetwater:** Navajo lad at St. Michael's.
- **Mary:** Irish maid.
- **Omney:** guide who went with English party (not coming).

## CH 1: PLANS FOR THE SOUTHWEST TRIP
- First day of summer vacation, Mrs. Vernon's home. Telegram from Gilroy in Denver; letter pending.
- Scout history: Blue Mountains NJ (first camp; Blue Beard's cave; rescued Gilroy from escaped convicts). Second summer: First Lake, Fulton Chain, Adirondacks. Third: Rockies (Estes Park). Patrol No. 1 (Julie, Betty, Joan, Ruth, Hester, Amy, Edith, Judith, Anne); No. 2 younger.
- Applicants for Southwest: Julie, Betty, Joan, Hester. Mrs. Blake and Mrs. Ward refuse.
- Gilroy's letter (typewritten, "My dear pals of the Rockies"): items list (rain and dew, tents, Japanese parasols, "ice near Gallinas Canyon"). Tally guides; Omney left. Route: Sunday train to Philadelphia, Chicago Limited; meet Gilroy in Chicago Monday noon. Julie flags train. Tally meets them at La Junta. Mention of Gilly's oculist and goggles. Ends "Consider yourselves paternally kissed upon the brows."
- Mrs. Vernon says Kansas City connection. Ice cream and layer cake.

## CH 2: JULIE'S SECRET AMBITION
- Chicago: Gilroy sings "Oh, say can you see." Luncheon, Michigan Boulevard, Lake Shore Drive, Edgewater Beach tea. Lake colors.
- Night train: Julie writes articles for *Elmertown Record* (her secret, earns money).
- Kansas City: Mr. Vernon meets them. Stop-over; 10:20 pm train; La Junta at 1 pm. Tally: "Me pooly well."
- Equipment list (khaki suits, wool suits, slickers, wool golf stockings, three wool underwear sets, rubber boots, hiking shoes, riding boots).
- Elk-skin boots: Gilroy wants them. Trinidad, Hotel The Cardenas.
- Tally: horses from Denver dealer failed; Indian in Raton Mountain area (Gray Mine road). Family makes elk-skin boots. Mr. Gilroy and Vernon buy boots (scouts 2 pairs each). Vernon gives extra $10. Squaw sells beaded moccasins.

## CH 3: ON THE OLD SANTA FÉ TRAIL
- Indian horse-trader: 9 ponies, 3 burros, $20–$30 each per month; freight from Gallup/Flagstaff/Williams. Insurance for three months.
- Leave Trinidad 4 am. Burro names: Slow Poke (tents), Spark (stove), Good-fer-Nuttin' ("Nuttin'"). Julie's pony White Star (white face spot). Joan's Sweetie. Tally's mule Stick.
- Raton Mountain, Sky-line trail. Forest Ranger Sanderson joins; going to Springer; fish; Gilroy & Vernon fish with him.
- Waterfall (~200 ft). Julie poses on a leaning pine; vines tear; she falls over ledge. Tally climbs down ("Julesafed!"). Gilroy with ammonia (Mrs. Vernon's vial). Julie faints, revives. Hester had run film through all 12 exposures.
- Note left on stick for Ranger. Ride on.

## CH 4: JULIE MAKES A CONQUEST
- Tally takes wrong trail; small lake (~1 mile). Hemlock beds (Betty, Hester). Julie and Joan fish; loon.
- 1 am: Tally sees Ranger Sanderson ride in on Snubby. Sanderson had gone to Santa Fé Trail, then back to Forks; took Cimarron Trail. Coffee with Tally; they sleep.
- Morning: scouts swim (cold). Julie asks Tally for fish pole; Sanderson in camp. Julie flirts; Joan teases ("Give Sandy time"). Gilroy and Sandy catch trout. Vernon: "Julie's made a conquest."
- Ride Red River trail to Springer. Sanderson's history talk: Santa Fé trail, Simpson's Rest, Fisher's Peak, Las Animas ("River of Lost Souls").

## CH 5: SANDY HAS HIS SAY
- Springer (~1,000 pop.). Burt absent; wire says he's at Castañeda Hotel, Las Vegas.
- Plan: Tally ships burros by freight; scouts ride ~70 miles via Wagon Mound.
- Route: State Reformatory, Colmor, Lake Charetts reservoir, Wagon Mound, Optimo, Valmora (TB sanatorium), Watrous, Mora/Sapello rivers, Shoemaker Canyon, Las Vegas.
- Castañeda Hotel: warm baths; late dinner.
- Reading room: Sanderson vs. Burt debate. Sanderson quotes Bursum Bill (Pueblo lands, water rights, 1858 confirmation). Mescalero bill. 1913 Supreme Court ruling on Indian statute of limitations. "The solution is water." Illustrated paper dated November 29, 1922.
- Mr. Gilroy eavesdrops. Vernon enters: "turned literary."
- Julie gives Burt her papers; writes long letter at desk; mails it. Joan pretends sleep.

## CH 6: WHAT HAPPENED IN THE PECOS FORESTS
- Captain uneasy about Julie–Burt talks.
- Las Vegas: three cities (ancient Spanish, Castañeda, Hot Springs). Gallinas Canyon: 60,000 tons ice/year.
- Pecos Forest: 750,000 acres; ~600 miles trails. Bernal Creek camp; night at Pecos River near Blanchard; Pecos town (8,000 ft). Mention of Panchuelo lookout.
- Sanderson & Burt go to Santa Fé; Ranger Johnson takes scouts (Apache Inn, Valley Ranch). Pecos Cañon; Baldy Pecos; Grass Mountain (branch station, Johnson & friend).
- View; Gilroy: "a hundred and eighty pounds" joke.
- Tally's Beaver and Porcupine tale (Julie writes it down). Next dawn: climb.

## CH 7: WHERE ARE THE BURROS?
- Ranger Oliver guides them to Lake Park; burros hobbled and packs cached at Lake Park. Winsor; camp on Pecos near Panchuelo.
- Panchuelo: burros gone. Tally finds tracks, pipe ash; two riders drove burros down-trail. Bridge over torrent; tributary; Tally takes his route alone with Colt revolver.
- Mrs. Vernon worries. Bishop's Lodge (Mr. Vernon registers). Sanderson hidden behind newspaper; leaves for Santa Fé for guides.
- 11:45 pm: Gilroy and Tally return with burros.

## CH 8: GILLY TURNS FOREST RANGER
- Gilroy's tale: smoke from Lake Park fire; Rangers Oliver and Johnson; 100,000-acre territory; firefighting; "Ruins" bowlder area; fire subdued by axes, spades, mats.
- Search for Tally fails. Gilroy bets Rangers Tally will catch outlaws alone.
- Tally refuses to finish tale ("Solly, Mees Jule").

## CH 9: TALLY AND THE RUSTLERS
- Tally's tale: hides horse, puts on moccasins. Finds camp by clearing; two thieves, Ben and Bill, with blooded horses and the burros.
- Captures Ben behind pine; gags and binds him. Bill tries to escape; Tally takes his revolver; ropes him ("Now tek rope f'om saddle").
- Tally feeds burros/horses; smothers fire. Forest fire behind them. Leads prisoners down-trail; scolds them.
- Forester's blaze reroutes him; reaches bridge; kisses horse's nose.
- Sanderson and forest detectives, plus the two New Yorkers who owned the stolen horses ($500 reward). Tally refuses reward ("belongs to um-m-m scout").

## CH 10: ANCIENT RUINS AND MODERN ROMANCE
- Sanderson returns; Adair and Chase join (with thoroughbreds Tally found).
- Route: Tesuque Creek, Tesuque Pueblo ("gods" pottery), Cuyamunque, Nambe (kiva, Nambe Falls), Escondillo, Sanctuario chapel, Chimayo (blankets), Truchas River camp, Trampas, Ranchos de Taos.
- Taos Pueblo: 7-story walls, seven kivas, ~400 natives. Captain guards against flirting; Betty's innocent "not their horses" joke.
- Ride back via Rio Grande: San Juan, Santa Cruz, Puye Ruins (1,600 rooms), Española, San Ildefonso.
- Santa Fé: Belnap Ranch (Sandy's friends stay there). Sights: Museum, Old Palace, Cathedral (1612), San Miguel church.

## CH 11: PADRE MIGUEL'S STORY
- Padre Miguel (88; 70 years at mission). Julie introduces him.
- Tales: Old Palace; Spanish lady avenging brother-in-law; the Fonda, customs house, prison; caravans; ute and comanche danger.
- Padre on Jemez; Isleta friar who wakes to warn of floods.
- Vernon privately wrote scouts' fathers; cars hired (Sanderson bargains). Plans: Bandelier, Frijoles, Painted Cave, Cochita, San Felipe, Tiffany Turquoise Mines, San Marcos ruins.
- Two cars: Sandy drives Julie/Hester/Gilroy/Chase; Tally drives Captain/Vernon/Betty/Joan/Burt/Adair.

## CH 12: JULIE'S TÊTE-À-TÊTE
- Jemez Forests; Frijoles Cañon "City of the Dead" cliff dwellings. Flowers (blood-red cactus, mountain pink).
- Week of trips: Tiffany mine, Bonanza, Ortiz placers, Aztec City, Chaco Cañon.
- Surprise: Anne, Judith, Amy arrive by train. Mrs. Ward changed mind due to Julie's articles.
- Alvarado Hotel, Albuquerque (University of NM above city; Sanderson graduated).
- Sandy's wish at Enchanted Mesa (Julie's "icy attitude"). Dance: Julie "thawing." Balcony tête-à-tête; Sandy wants letters; Julie promises to think it over. Mrs. Vernon interrupts. "Here's my post office address—Julie, dear!"

## CH 13: THE ENCHANTED MESA
- Sandy and New Yorkers leave. Burt goes with scouts to Gallup.
- Laguna: Mr. Balmore advises wagons not horses. Four-in-hands; Tally left behind.
- Painted-scene; sheep; mirage (mountain vanishes); "By the Great-horned Spoon!" (Vernon).
- Acoma: pueblo on mesa 400+ ft; ladders; church 40 years to build, walls 10 ft thick.
- Council: Arizona limited to one month. Plan: Painted Desert, Petrified Forests, Grand Cañon, Hualapai reservation; Prescott Junction; Salt River and Gila reservations; Apache Trail; Roosevelt Dam; Tucson; Sunset Route to Houston; steamer from Galveston to NY. Burt: "Only wish I was a Girl Scout."

## CH 14: AT ST. MICHAEL'S MISSION
- Local train Laguna→Gallup. Conductor praises Cañon de Chelly and White House ruin. Burt leaves for Zuñi with Zuñi guide.
- El Navajo hotel, Gallup. Manager Mr. Walters; "I'll wear the cap."
- Tally's freight arrives after midnight. Walters: sell burros in Gallup; buy pack-horses at mission; hire Navajo guide. Lease: burros left at Gallup; monthly hire paid.
- Motor cars to St. Michael's: rack for tents and stove. Tally + Gilroy + Vernon ride horses.
- Mission: Father in charge; Navajo school; Mother Superior; supper; vespers.
- Games: John Sweetwater's "White Feather" nine-peg tent trick; Nature Game.

## CH 15: THE PAINTED DESERT
- Julie writes Sandy; Captain's advice ("general topics only"). Julie plans to be a writer.
- Three pack-horses and Lo (Lorenzo). Ganado trading post; Lorenzo Hubbell "King of Northern Arizona." San Francisco Mountains.
- Second night on desert: cold; fires. Simoon (sandstorm); Anne's alkali dust. Joan's horse hit by object, plunges into pit; she saves horse.
- Ream's Cañon (Keam's): trader; Kit Carson monument; school; permits.
- Moki villages on tufa mesas. Lo: "for Lo there was but one world... Navajo Land." Lo leaves for mission.
- Adamana: Tally wants rest; Gilroy: no lounging.

## CH 16: THE REGION OF THE PETRIFIED FORESTS
- Forests: first (6 miles), second (3 mi SE, ~2,000 acres), Chalcedony Park (13 mi SW), Rainbow Forest (2 mi NW of third). Gilroy's flood story (trees, Inland Lake).
- Eagle's Head; Petrified Bridge (111 ft).
- Adamana host advises Lava Fields, Sunset Crater, Diablo Cañon, Meteorite Mountain, Williams, Flagstaff.
- Julie's *Record* articles (Sunset Crater; Meteorite Mountain: 200-ft mound, mile-deep bowl, 40 acres; Cañon Diablo, 250-ft bridge).
- Lo's, trader's, host's invitations declined. Flagstaff: Lowell Observatory at night; Montezuma's Castle (47 mi south) declined.
- Telegram from Trinidad dealer: "Ship back freight collect."
- Williams: horses shipped home; Tally sells three pack-horses ($30 each; $90) and camp outfit; profit split 50-50 with Gilroy.

## CH 17: BRIGHT ANGEL TRAIL
- Train Williams→Grand Cañon. Sarcastic tourist; El Tovar Hotel (avoided; they camp at John Bass Camp).
- First view at sunset: Betty sobs; purple fade.
- Sunrise; Gilroy: "frying bacon."
- Betty afraid; Amy and Hester volunteer to stay; Joan refuses; Mrs. Vernon: all go down.
- Bright Angel Trail: 23 tourists. Woman Lizzie demands return, then continues. Julie's mule at a bend: "half of me on the down-trail." Indian Gardens; Jacob's Ladder; Devil's Corkscrew (Vernon: "devil of a corkscrew").
- Noon at river bottom; camp on sand. Next day: Bright Angel Creek, Phantom Ranch, Ribbon Falls; Hermit trail, Santa Maria Spring, Lion Cañon, Hermit Cabins, Cape Butte, Tonto Trail. Three days in the Cañon.
- Specimens: 240 bird species; cacti (hedgehog, barrel, cholla, ocotillo "Devil's Claw"); flowers (phacelia, Arizona dandelion). Boxes shipped to Elmertown.
- Gilroy's Adirondack title dispute; his lawyer; court opens September. Must leave; all return home via Arizona and Gulf.
- Tally: "Don' leaf Tally outen dat mountain climb." Joan: other mountains next summer. Julie: "So _he_ says." (Last line.)
